chapter: Cab Calloway, Harlem and New York musicians
title: New York's guitar and banjo players: Bobby Johnson, Truehart, Clarence Holiday
summary: On arriving in New York, Danny noticed virtuoso banjoists struggling while rhythm players like John Truehart and Clarence Holiday anchored big bands.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: I found when I got to New York... I looked around and saw all the virtuoso guitar players (there wasn't many [?] banjo players, and they weren't doing much. They were with tramp bands, or they were working in dives and... I saw Banjo Bernie come through, and I saw Speed, Speedy... Speedy worked with Luckey Roberts and them. And I looked in the big bands, and in Charlie Johnson's band was Bobby Johnson, who was neat, cool, clean, didn't have too much to say, tended to business -- a banjo player. There was guys greater than him, but he was in Charlie Johnson's band.
There was [John] Truehart in Chick Webb's band, who was the master and the boss of rhythm. Everybody remarked how great he was.
Yeah. He was (?), the poor boy died of TB. But he was a master. He would never take a solo, maybe a little break here.
And there was Clarence Holiday with Fletcher Henderson's band.
Yes, Billie Holiday's father. He was immaculate, wore them hundred and some suits, at that time

them Coleman Hawkins suits with the hand-stitched lapels, and immaculate hats and shirts, and neat and cool. And he was no virtuoso, but he was the pivot in the band; he was the solid foundation in the band.
